groups.title: Buttons
groups.intro: Variant sets how loud a button is. Theme sets what it means. Never use theme to create emphasis.

items.name: Sizes
items.note: Small is the default. Filmmakers System is dense, and small suits it. Use a different size only for the cases below.
rules: Use btn-sm unless one of the other rows applies.
Use btn-xs in table rows, inline row actions and compact toolbars.
Keep one size within a group of buttons.

items.name: Primary
items.note: The one most important action on the screen. It takes the customer’s primary colour.
rules: At most one primary button per screen. Where two compete, pick the one most people take, or make both secondary.
Primary means “most important thing here”. It never means safe, confirm, new or recommended.
On a dark or brand-coloured surface, use btn-solid theme-inverse instead.

items.name: Secondary
items.note: Actions that matter but are not the main one: Cancel, Export, Save draft.
rules: Use as many as the screen needs. Most actions are secondary.
Never use btn-outline theme-primary: it becomes a second primary.
On a dark or brand-coloured surface, use btn-outline theme-inverse.

items.name: Tertiary
items.note: Quiet page-level actions, in menus and in toolbars: Discard, Learn more, Back. For actions on one item in a list, use a Row action.
rules: Icon-only buttons are always tertiary. They are allowed only for overflow menus, close controls, and toolbar actions with a well-known icon (search, filter).
Every icon-only button needs an accessible name (aria-label) and a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus.
The hit target is at least 44×44px. Icon-only buttons are never destructive.

items.name: Row action
items.note: Actions on one item in a dense list: Edit, Duplicate, View as applicant, Copy/Move, Messages. Primary colour shows where to act on each row; text and extra small keep it quiet.
rules: Only on an item: a table cell, a list row or a row gutter. Page-level quiet actions are Tertiary.
Always has a text label. Never icon only.
Same set, same order, on every row. Always visible, never revealed on hover.
At most three, then a “More” row action that opens the overflow menu. Never destructive.
The label must meet 4.5:1 on the row background for every customer primary.

items.note: For actions that remove or destroy something. Red because of what it does. How loud it is depends on where it sits.

Solid danger is only for confirming a destructive action in a dialog.
Label the action with what it does (Remove, Delete). Never icon only.

items.name: Client zone
items.note: A secondary button whose icon takes the client zone accent. It tells people they are in an area that clients, or others outside the team, can see.
rules: Use it on every such action inside a client zone. An inconsistent signal is worse than none.
Never use it outside client zones, and never on solid or text buttons.
It is never the only signal. The page itself must also say the content is visible to clients.

Client zone is Bootstrap orange-500 (#ff6800). Accessibility: the icon is about 2.9:1 on the white button, just under the 3:1 WCAG 2.1 AA needs for icons (1.4.11). It still passes overall because the label carries the meaning, but the colour itself fails. Decide: keep orange-500, or use orange-600 (#cd5100, about 4.4:1, passes).

rules: Every button in a group is the same size.

Medium and large are not used for groups.

items.name: Text labels
items.note: Two or three closely related actions on the same object, joined into one control. The joining is the meaning: these actions belong together.
rules: Two or three actions. That is the whole range.
Every button uses btn-outline theme-secondary. No solid buttons, no text buttons, no second variant.
Labels are short and name the action.
Where one action deserves more weight, put it outside the group as a separate button.

items.name: Icon only
items.note: A group where every button is icon only. Use only when each icon is well known.
rules: Every button is icon only. Never mix icon-only and text buttons in one group.
Each button has an accessible name (aria-label) and a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus.

items.name: Split button
items.note: One action with variants: a text button plus an icon-only menu trigger that belongs to it. This is the only group that may mix a text button and an icon button.
rules: The trigger opens variants of the same action (Save / Save and new, Generate PDF / CSV).
The trigger has an accessible name that says what the menu holds.

items.name: With an overflow menu
items.classes: btn-group > btn-outline theme-secondary + btn-icon menu trigger
items.note: Four or more actions on the same object: keep the one or two used most in the group, and move the rest to an overflow menu at the end of the group.
rules: The overflow trigger is the last button in the group, in the same outline style and size.
It is icon only, with an accessible name (aria-label="More actions") and a tooltip.
Like the split-button trigger, it is an allowed exception to “never mix text and icon-only buttons”.
Destructive actions go in the overflow menu with a text label.
A screen that needs many actions on one object is a hierarchy problem. Lower the emphasis rather than adding buttons.

items.name: Vertical
items.note: Groups are horizontal. Stack them only in narrow layouts where horizontal does not fit.
rules: Below the tablet breakpoint, a group that does not fit stacks. It never scrolls or truncates.
Never stretch a group to fill its container. Icon buttons would grow into squares.

items.name: Accessibility
items.note: What every group needs, whatever its version.
rules: The container has role="group" (or role="toolbar" for a toolbar) and an aria-label that names what the group does.
Every button is a <button type="button">. Not a link, not a span.
Buttons are reachable by keyboard in visual order.
Focus is visible on each button, including where borders are shared.

items.name: Not allowed
items.note: A button group is for actions only.
rules: All-primary groups, or any btn-solid button inside a group.
Mixed variants or themes in one group, or btn-text inside a group.
Destructive and non-destructive actions in the same group.
More than three actions in a group.
Switching views or content sets: use tabs.
A yes/no or on/off choice: use a switch or checkbox. Choosing one value: use a radio group.
Navigation: use links.
Unrelated actions grouped together. Separate them.

items.name: Open decisions
items.note: Not yet decided in the Button groups pattern. Do not build these until they are.
rules: Segmented controls: whether we use them at all.
Selected state: only needed if segmented controls are adopted. Solid secondary is banned, so a selected state needs defining.
Toolbars: whether a toolbar of several groups is a pattern we use, and how groups are separated in one.

groups.title: Checkbox
groups.intro: Choose any number of options. The input sits beside its label, joined by for and id.

items.name: Checkbox
items.note: Replace. The input is a sibling of the label, not nested inside it; pair them with for/id. Help text goes in a form-text below. One exception, inside a menu item (FRM-11): the input is nested in the label so the whole row is the hit target, and it drops .check-sm. UNRESOLVED - whether the nested form is permitted or the menu item should carry for/id like every other checkbox.

groups.title: Chips
groups.intro: Removable tokens, one per applied filter.

items.name: Chip
items.note: Added. One chip per applied filter, each with a dismiss button that resets that filter to its page default. Only used in the chips variant of SF-1, which is not in production use yet.

flags.text: Accessibility: the dismiss button is 16×16px. That passes WCAG 2.1 AA, which has no target-size rule at AA, and very likely WCAG 2.2 AA through its spacing exception. It fails the Buttons guideline’s 44×44px rule for icon-only buttons. Decide whether to widen the hit area (at least 24×24px) without changing how the chip looks.

Accessibility: passes on text contrast (about 15.6:1, Bootstrap’s default body text), accessible names (“Remove the Status filter”), keyboard use and not relying on colour. Its focus ring is Bootstrap’s default, about 1.9:1 against white (the open focus ring decision in Colour).

groups.title: Combobox
groups.intro: One control for every filter and sort: radio items for one value, checkboxes for many.

items.name: Combobox
items.note: Replace. Multi-select filter: the toggle shows the label and the selection (“Language: 2 selected”), the menu holds one checkbox per value, and a .combobox-search input appears once the list passes six entries. One control for every filter: single-value filters carry radio items, multi-value filters checkbox items, and the toggle always reads label plus value. Replaces the native select the product used before (FRM-2, retired), including the Sort by control. Two deviations to settle: the checkbox is nested inside label.menu-item rather than paired by for/id (see FRM-9), and it resets --bs-theme-bg / --bs-theme-contrast because a themed .menu parent would otherwise paint the unchecked box in the menu's own fill.
rules: The toggle always reads label: value, for example “Status: Active” or “Language: 2 selected”, so a filter reads as a sentence.
A filter that differs from its default is weight 600. No colour, no badge.
One value: radio items, and the menu closes on pick. Several values: checkbox items, and the menu stays open.
More than six options: a find field appears at the top, with a “No … matches” line when nothing matches.
Filters apply on change. There is no Apply button. The menu closes on an outside click.
Use the Combobox for every filter and for Sort by. The native select is only for forms.

groups.title: Search and filter
groups.intro: One filter bar for every list page: search, filters, sorting and a result count.

items.name: Search and filter bar
items.note: One filter bar for every list page. Search first, up to three inline filters, the rest behind More filters, sorting last, and the count on its own row. Each filter reads as a sentence, and the bar hands the filtered rows back to the page.

flags.text: Clear filters uses btn-text theme-primary. That combination is the Row action, which the Buttons guideline allows only on an item in a list. Decide whether Clear filters is an exception or becomes Tertiary (btn-text theme-secondary).
The prototype opens Sort by with menu-end, which this Bootstrap build does not have. Use data-bs-placement="bottom-end".

rules: Order: search, inline filters (up to three), More filters, Clear filters, then Sort by at the far end.
Every filter is a Combobox reading label: value. Applied filters are weight 600, and More filters shows how many of its filters are applied.
Clear filters appears only when a search or filter is applied, and resets all of them.
Filters apply on change. No Apply button.
The count row always shows, with the same range as the table footer, for example “1-3 of 4 coworkers”.

The bar fits filters to its width: each filter that no longer fits moves into More filters, then none are inline. When More filters and Sort by would overlap, both become icon buttons in one Button group (filter and sort icons, btn-outline theme-secondary as every Button group is, each with an accessible name and tooltip), and Clear filters moves to the bottom of the More filters popover. The icon buttons never change size and show no count; the applied count is in the filter button’s accessible name. On these widths the popover and menus fill the bar’s width.
Pages with only two or three filters never show More filters. The bar adapts by removing, not adding.
The bar sits on the bg-1 surface at the top of the card that holds the list.

groups.title: Actions
groups.intro: Where row and item actions live, and how they are laid out.

items.name: Action gutter
items.note: Replace. Row actions are always visible, never revealed on hover. The gutter tint is --bs-bg-1 on every page; the buttons inside are always CNT-13.

flags.text: Edit uses the Row action button (Buttons). Remove is never in the gutter itself: it sits in the More overflow, as decided in review.

items.example: Season 14: Erste Runde

items.name: Row actions
items.note: One component for every row action group. Each action is a boolean prop (messages, edit, duplicate, viewAsApplicant, copyMove, unsubscribe, remove, more), so pages cannot drift. layout="stack" fills an Action gutter; layout="inline" sits in a table cell. The v3 pipe separators are gone: spacing comes from flex gap.

flags.text: Changed from RowActions.dc.html: the prototype’s More had no menu, it allowed up to seven visible actions, and it put Unsubscribe and Remove beside the others as bare danger buttons. Here More opens a real menu, at most three actions show, and the destructive ones are inside More, per the Buttons and Destructive actions guidelines. Decided in review: Remove goes under More, even when it is reversible.

rules: Every action is a Row action: btn-text theme-primary btn-xs, icon plus text label. Edit is a link (a) because it navigates; the rest are buttons.
Fixed order on every row: Messages, Edit, Duplicate, View as applicant, Copy/Move, then More. Turning an action off never reorders the rest.
At most three actions show. Each page chooses which three; the choice is the same on every row of that page. The rest go into More, which is always last and always opens a .menu.
Unsubscribe and Remove are never bare controls. They go last in More, after a divider, as menu-item theme-danger, and follow Destructive actions (undo if reversible, confirm if not).
More carries an accessible name with the row, e.g. “More actions for Season 14: Erste Runde”, so repeated triggers are distinguishable.
Stack has no gap between buttons; inline uses an 8px gap.
